title: Graphs of large girth and large chromatic number: Erdős, Mycielski, and the fractional chromatic number of Mycielski graphs
abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of three classical results on graphs with large chromatic number. (1) Erdős' 1959 theorem: for every g and k there is a finite graph with girth greater than g and chromatic number greater than k, in the structural form given by the probabilistic argument (for every ε > 0 and all large n, a graph on n vertices with girth greater than g whose independent sets have fewer than εn vertices). (2) Mycielski's 1955 construction M(G): it preserves and reflects triangle-freeness, M(G) is (k+1)-colourable exactly when G is k-colourable, χ(M(G)) = χ(G) + 1 for every finite G, and iterating from K₂ gives triangle-free graphs with 3·2ⁿ − 1 vertices and chromatic number n + 2. (3) Larsen, Propp and Ullman (1995): for the fractional chromatic number χ_f (least total weight of a fractional colouring by independent sets), χ_f(M(G)) = χ_f(G) + 1/χ_f(G) for every finite graph G with at least one vertex. Version 2 adds (2) and (3); the statements of version 1 are unchanged. Mathlib has girth and chromatic number but none of these theorems, and no fractional chromatic number.
